newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish military vows to stay out of politics.
newsitem.headline: Turkish military vows to stay out of politics.

text.p: Turkey's chief of staff Ismail Hakki Karadayi said on Friday the army would keep out of politics despite its public opposition to the policies of the Islamist-led government, the Anatolian news agency reported.

Karadayi said the army -- which has ousted three civilian governments since 1960 -- was watching political developments closely and demanded parliament act to resolve the political deadlock gripping Ankara.

"The Turkish armed forces exist completely outside politics and they will stay outside," Karadayi was quoted as saying. "There are some developments in our country against the basic constitutional properties of our republic to which our people and our armed forces are extremely sensitive."
"Nobody can remain insensible and impartial in the face of this. But the place to resolve this is parliament. We believe that everything can and should be solved under that roof."

The army top brass is expected to confront Erbakan at a National Security Council meeting on Saturday with his failure to implement an anti-Islamist crackdown demanded by the fiercely secularist military two months ago.

Erbakan, the first Islamist to lead modern Turkey, and pro-Western government ally Tansu Ciller hastily arranged a meeting amid reports the government was close to collapse. Ciller earlier denied a press story that she would pull out of the alliance at the behest of the powerful army.

A war of attrition between Welfare and the army reached a new height on Thursday when the Islamists threatened legal action against a middle-ranking general who had verbally abused Erbakan in comments seen on national television.
General Osman Ozbek called Erbakan a "pimp" for going on pilgrimage to the Moslem holy city of Mecca as the guest of conservative Saudi King Fahd.
Karadayi called the incident a "one-off, personal case", and said any necessary measures would be taken.
"Such incidents are evaluated and if necessary, within our own internal discipline system, the required precautions will be taken. Legally this is entirely our own concern," he said.
